faqs.question: What does "propose karna" actually mean in Hindi?
faqs.answer: In everyday Indian usage it almost always means asking someone to be your girlfriend or boyfriend, not asking them to marry you. Hindi has no native verb for the romantic ask — McGregor's Oxford Hindi-English Dictionary glosses प्रस्ताव as an introduction or a motion for discussion — which is why the English loan is used.

faqs.question: Which Hindi line should I send if I just want her to be my girlfriend?
faqs.answer: क्या तुम मेरे साथ आगे बढ़ना चाहोगी? (Kya tum mere saath aage badhna chaahogi?) — "Would you want to move forward with me?" It is in the तुम register and it names a future thing she can agree to, which a compliment cannot.

faqs.question: Should I use तुम, आप or तू?
faqs.answer: Use whichever one she already uses with you. तुम is the ordinary register between peers, आप creates respectful distance and is permanent in many families, and तू is either very intimate or rude depending on the relationship. A proposal is the wrong moment to change register.

faqs.question: Can a woman use these lines?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the first-person verb agreement changed. कह रहा हूँ becomes कह रही हूँ, कर रहा becomes कर रही, and करूँगा becomes करूँगी. The lines addressed to her stay the same.

faqs.question: Is there a Hindi verb that means "to propose" the way English uses it?
faqs.answer: Not for a romantic proposal. प्रस्ताव is the formal word — a motion, a proposal for discussion — and in the Hindi Dependency Treebank all 230 sentences containing it are parliamentary or commercial. The ask has to be carried by the question itself.

faqs.question: What if she does not answer at all?
faqs.answer: That is usually a misfire rather than a refusal: the ask was read as banter, or there was no moment in which answering was possible. Line 3, मैं मज़ाक नहीं कर रहा, मैं सच कह रहा हूँ, exists to close off exactly that reading.

faqs.question: When is Propose Day 2027?
faqs.answer: Monday 8 February 2027. It is the second day of Valentine week, after Rose Day on Sunday 7 February, and the week runs eight dated days to Valentine's Day on Sunday 14 February.

faqs.question: Do I have to write it in Devanagari?
faqs.answer: No. Send it in whichever script she types in — the Devanagari here is given with a Roman transliteration for that reason. The script choice is covered in full on the propose message in Hindi page.

faqs.question: How many of these lines should I send at once?
faqs.answer: Three: the setup, the ask, and the line that says what happens after her answer. Sent as one message rather than three, because only the first one shows in a notification preview.

faqs.question: Which SubhSandesh page fits a girlfriend proposal?
faqs.answer: The romantic "I love you" page at /love-gf, which is 1,173 pages and 23.2% of all 5,061 built platform-wide across 20 page types. The /proposal scrapbook is built for the marriage question and is too much page for "will you be my girlfriend".

faqs.question: Were these Hindi lines checked by a native speaker?
faqs.answer: No. Every word was checked against the Hindi Dependency Treebank or the 16,475-sentence Tatoeba Hindi corpus, and every headword against a Hindi-English dictionary, but no native speaker reviewed them. Lines whose forms were not attested were cut rather than published.

faqs.question: How is this page different from the other Hindi propose pages?
faqs.answer: This one is the hub: it answers the whole question briefly and then routes you to whichever of the ten Hindi pages matches what you are actually doing — a method, a message, a couplet, a greeting or a joke. The depth lives on those pages, not here.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Propose Girlfriend in Hindi: The One Line, Then Where to Go

To propose to your girlfriend in Hindi, ask one question in the pronoun she already uses with you, then stop talking: **क्या तुम मेरे साथ आगे बढ़ना चाहोगी?** (*Kya tum mere saath aage badhna chaahogi?* — "Would you want to move forward with me?"). A proposal does not describe how you feel. It is an act performed by saying it, which is why it can never be true or false — only successful or botched.

Two SubhSandesh numbers set the frame, both platform-wide across 5,061 personalised pages and 20 page types: 91.2% of started pages are published and shared (4,615 of 5,061), and 38.7% of creators password-protect the page before sending it (1,961 of 5,061). Propose Day 2027 falls on Monday 8 February.

Below: which of ten Hindi pages you need, six lines with the register marked, and the four conditions a proposal has to meet.

## What makes a proposal a performative, not a sentence about feelings

A proposal is a [performative utterance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performative_utterance): saying it is doing it. The words do not report a fact about the world — they ask the world to change until it matches the words.

Speech act theory calls this the direction of fit. Katsuya Yamori's 2019 paper in the *IDRiM Journal* separates the two: a [constative utterance is word-to-world](https://www.idrimjournal.com/article/11663-disaster-information-from-the-viewpoint-of-speech-act-theory-constative-performative-and-declarative-utterances) — "this is a pencil" holds until you find it is pencil-shaped chocolate, and then you change the words. A performative runs the other way, world-to-word: nothing makes "please open the door" true or false.

Hold two Hindi sentences against that test. **तुम मुझे बहुत पसंद हो** (*tum mujhe bahut pasand ho*, "I like you a lot") reports something. **क्या तुम मेरे साथ आगे बढ़ना चाहोगी?** does something. Only the second is a proposal, and it is the one most people leave out.

## Which of the ten Hindi pages you need, decided in nine questions

Ten SubhSandesh pages answer some version of this query in Hindi, and they are not versions of each other. Stop at the first yes.

1. **You want a method, not words** — [how to propose to your girlfriend in Hindi](/blog/how-to-propose-girlfriend-in-hindi).
2. **You are typing one message to one named person today** — [propose message in Hindi](/blog/propose-message-in-hindi).
3. **You want a couplet and can tell a sher from a stanza** — [propose girlfriend shayari](/blog/propose-girlfriend-shayari).
4. **You mix Hindi and English when you text her** — [Propose Day quotes in Hindi and English](/blog/propose-day-quotes-hindi-english).
5. **You want a standalone quotable line** — [Propose Day quotes in Hindi](/blog/propose-day-quotes-in-hindi).
6. **You are sending a greeting, not asking anything** — [Propose Day wishes in Hindi](/blog/propose-day-wishes-in-hindi), or, if it is only for her, [Propose Day wishes for a girlfriend in Hindi](/blog/propose-day-wishes-for-girlfriend-in-hindi).
7. **She is already your wife** — [Propose Day quotes for a wife in Hindi](/blog/propose-day-quotes-for-wife-in-hindi).
8. **You want her to laugh, not to decide** — [Propose Day jokes in Hindi](/blog/propose-day-jokes-in-hindi).
9. **You are not certain what the day is** — [Propose Day meaning in Hindi](/blog/propose-day-meaning-in-hindi). Short answer: Monday 8 February 2027, the second of Valentine week's eight dated days, which opens on Rose Day, Sunday 7 February.

Nothing fits? Then you are in the right place: what is left is the ask.

## Six lines that do six different jobs, with the register marked

Every word below is attested in the Hindi Dependency Treebank or the Tatoeba Hindi corpus, both linked at the end. None of it is film dialogue, lyric or forward.

### 1. सुनो, मुझे तुमसे कुछ पूछना है।

**Roman and English:** *Suno, mujhe tumse kuchh poochhna hai.* — "Listen, I have something to ask you."

**Register:** तुम. A woman says the same words.

**What it does:** it opens the procedure. An act needs a recognised one before it can come off, and this tells her an ask is coming.

**Use it when:** before anything else. पूछना takes से for the person asked — तुमसे, not तुमको.

### 2. क्या तुम मेरे साथ आगे बढ़ना चाहोगी?

**Roman and English:** *Kya tum mere saath aage badhna chaahogi?* — "Would you want to move forward with me?"

**Register:** तुम. To a man, चाहोगे.

**What it does:** this is the act. It names a future thing she can agree to, which a compliment never does.

**Use it when:** straight after line 1. The frame *क्या तुम … चाहोगी?* is attested in ordinary conversational Hindi.

### 3. मैं मज़ाक नहीं कर रहा, मैं सच कह रहा हूँ।

**Roman and English:** *Main mazaak nahin kar raha, main sach kah raha hoon.* — "I'm not joking, I'm telling you the truth."

**Register:** तुम context. A woman says कर रही and कह रही हूँ.

**What it does:** it closes off the joke reading. Some proposals are never refused at all — they are taken as banter and never answered.

**Use it when:** you two joke constantly, or you hinted before and she laughed.

### 4. तुम जो भी कहो, मैं तुमसे ऐसे ही बात करूँगा।

**Roman and English:** *Tum jo bhi kaho, main tumse aise hi baat karoonga.* — "Whatever you say, I'll talk to you exactly the same way."

**Register:** तुम. A woman says करूँगी.

**What it does:** it commits you to what happens after her answer — the part that decides whether she can answer honestly at all.

**Use it when:** in the same message as the ask. Said later it is damage control.

### 5. आप मेरे बारे में एक बार सोचिए।

**Roman and English:** *Aap mere baare mein ek baar sochiye.* — "Think about me, once."

**Register:** आप. The shift changes the grammar: in आप the natural ask stops being a question and becomes a polite imperative.

**What it does:** it asks for consideration, not a decision — what आप distance is for.

**Use it when:** आप is already what you two use. Never promote her to आप for the occasion.

### 6. तू मेरे साथ है या नहीं?

**Roman and English:** *Tu mere saath hai ya nahin?* — "Are you with me, or not?"

**Register:** तू, the most intimate form and the most dangerous.

**What it does:** nothing but the ask. No setup, no softening, no room to think.

**Use it when:** तू is already how you speak to each other. If you have never used it with her, do not start here.

## The four conditions, and which one your proposal is failing

A performative cannot be true or false. It can only come off or misfire, and what has to be in place for it to come off are its felicity conditions.

Chusni Hadiati's 2019 study in *Theory and Practice in Language Studies* sets out [the four conditions an utterance has to meet](https://www.academypublication.com/issues2/tpls/vol09/06/13.pdf): preparatory, propositional content, sincerity, essential. Her example is a promise: "I would come to your house" is not one, because propositional content requires a future act and *would* does not predicate one; "I will come to your house" does.

Run a proposal through the same four and the failure modes stop being vague.

**Preparatory** — you are the right person and this is a moment she can answer in. A group chat fails here, whatever the wording.

**Propositional content** — the sentence must name a future act. "मुझे तुम्हारी याद आती है" names a present feeling, so it cannot be accepted or refused.

**Sincerity** — you mean it. That is what line 3 secures.

**Essential** — she recognises the utterance as the ask. Nothing you have not said counts, however clearly you feel it.

## Which ask, which line, which page

One row per ask. Every SubhSandesh figure below is platform-wide across 20 page types, never measured on proposal pages.

| What you are actually asking | Register | The Hindi line | SubhSandesh page, and what is measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| Will you be my girlfriend? | तुम | क्या तुम मेरे साथ आगे बढ़ना चाहोगी? | `/love-gf` — 1,173 pages, 23.2% of all 5,061 built |
| Will you think about it? | आप | आप मेरे बारे में एक बार सोचिए। | `/love-gf` — most-viewed template, 16,902 views, 30.1% of 56,152 |
| Will you marry me? | तुम or आप | covered in the how-to page, not here | `/proposal` — no page-level figure exists at all |
| I am asking again, after a no | तुम | तुम जो भी कहो, मैं तुमसे ऐसे ही बात करूँगा। | `/apology-dashboard` — 1,347 pages, 26.6% platform-wide |

Read row three carefully: it is where this traffic gets misrouted. In Indian usage *propose karna* almost always means asking someone to be your girlfriend, not to marry you — and Hindi has no native verb for it. McGregor's *Oxford Hindi-English Dictionary* glosses प्रस्ताव as an introduction, a proposal for discussion, a motion; in the Hindi Dependency Treebank all 230 sentences containing it are parliamentary or commercial. The English loan fills an empty slot.

So the [Will-You-Marry-Me proposal scrapbook](/proposal), which ends in a YES button that grows every time she dodges it, is the wrong template for most people who typed this query: it is built for the marriage question. Asking her to be your girlfriend, the [romantic "I love you" page](/love-gf) is the right size — 1,173 pages, 23.2% of everything built platform-wide. Asking again after a fight or a refusal, the [apology page](/apology-dashboard) is the honest one.

## When the Hindi line is the wrong choice, and when our page is

If the two of you have run in English since the day you met, a Hindi sentence for the biggest question you have asked reads as a costume. Say it in whatever language your arguments happen in.

And a built page is the wrong container while the question is open. 48.4% of views platform-wide land on a phone (27,185 of 56,152), so she is reading standing somewhere, with a link between her and your question — one more step at the moment you wanted none.

The median gap between a page's first save and its last edit is 2.4 hours, sampled on `/apology-dashboard`, n=1,348. Past a point, editing is avoidance. Take lines 1, 2 and 4, read them aloud, send them as one message.

A page earns its place after a yes, or when the ask is marriage. Not before.

## Sources

- Katsuya Yamori, [Disaster Information from the Viewpoint of Speech Act Theory](https://www.idrimjournal.com/article/11663-disaster-information-from-the-viewpoint-of-speech-act-theory-constative-performative-and-declarative-utterances), *IDRiM Journal* 9(1):40–55, 25 July 2019.
- Chusni Hadiati, [Felicity Conditions of the Speech Acts in Banyumasan Daily Conversation](https://www.academypublication.com/issues2/tpls/vol09/06/13.pdf), *Theory and Practice in Language Studies* 9(6):700–705, June 2019.
- Hautli, Sulger and Butt, [Adding an Annotation Layer to the Hindi/Urdu Treebank](https://journals.colorado.edu/index.php/lilt/article/view/1263), *Linguistic Issues in Language Technology* 7, 2012 — abstract only.
- [UD Hindi HDTB](https://universaldependencies.org/treebanks/hi_hdtb/index.html) — the treebank used to check attested forms.
- [Tatoeba Hindi corpus](https://tatoeba.org/en/downloads), 16,475 sentences — for the second-person forms a news treebank lacks.
